name: The avadhūta's twenty-four teachers

definitions.definition: The twenty-four teachers from whose ways the avadhūta brāhmaṇa learned freedom, told to King Yadu: earth (forbearance; its mountains and trees: living for others), air (content with bare sustenance; unattached among objects), sky (the self pervasive and untouched), water (purity that purifies), fire (taking all without taint; the Lord in all forms), moon (changes belong to the body), sun (taking and giving without attachment; one appearing many), pigeon (ruin by excessive attachment), python (accepting what comes), ocean (unmoved by gain and loss), moth (lured by forms to ruin), honeybee (begging a little from many; taking the essence of all scriptures; not hoarding), elephant (bound by touch of the female), honey-gatherer (hoarded wealth enjoyed by others), deer (lured by song), fish (the tongue), Piṅgalā (hope is misery, hopelessness bliss), osprey (possession invites attack), child (carefree bliss), maiden with bangles (live alone), arrow-maker (one-pointed absorption), serpent (homeless solitude), spider (the Lord emits and withdraws the world), wasp (one becomes what one dwells on). His own body is a further teacher of dispassion; knowledge from one teacher alone is not firm, for Brahman is sung in many ways.
Bodhya names six teachers — Piṅgalā, the osprey, the snake, the bee, the arrow-maker and the maiden (Mahābhārata 12.171.61).

notes: List verified in the local Bhāgavata e-text (11.7.33-34). The six teachers of Bodhya are a subset (Piṅgalā, osprey, serpent, bee, arrow-maker, maiden).

definitions.definition: The liberated wanderer who has shaken off all ties, behaves like a child, madman or dullard, is untouched by desire and learns from all beings.
The one beyond hope, vāsanā, meditation and ego, defined syllable by syllable in the Avadhūta Gītā.

Knowledge, action and devotion are the only means; knowledge suits those disgusted with action, action those still desirous, devotion those with faith in the Lord's stories who are neither disgusted nor over-attached; action is done until disgust or faith arises.

relations.note: the Devī Gītā also names action, knowledge and devotion as the three paths and calls devotion the easiest

definitions.definition: Action, knowledge and devotion lead to liberation; devotion is the easiest, being mental and paining neither body nor mind.

Eight chief siddhis residing in the Lord (aṇimā, mahimā, laghimā, prāpti, prākāmya, īśitā, vaśitā, fulfilment of desire) and ten from the guṇas (freedom from hunger and thirst, far hearing and seeing, speed of mind, taking any form, entering another body, dying at will, sporting with the gods, accomplishing one's resolve, unobstructed command), with lesser ones such as knowing the three times and others' minds; all are obstacles for one seeking the Lord.

name: Twelve yamas and twelve niyamas (Uddhava Gītā)

definitions.definition: Yamas: non-violence, truth, non-stealing, non-attachment, modesty, non-accumulation, faith in dharma, celibacy, silence, steadiness, forbearance, fearlessness. Niyamas: purity (outer and inner), recitation, austerity, fire-offering, faith, hospitality, worship of the Lord, pilgrimage, acting for others, contentment, service of the teacher.

name: Ten yamas and ten niyamas (Devī Gītā)

definitions.definition: Yamas: non-violence, truth, non-stealing, celibacy, compassion, uprightness, forbearance, fortitude, moderate food, purity. Niyamas: austerity, contentment, faith, charity, worship of the deity, hearing the settled doctrine, modesty, discernment, mantra repetition, oblation.

Kṛṣṇa redefines some thirty virtues and states inwardly (calm = intellect fixed on the Lord; strength = breath control; heaven = rise of sattva; the friend = the teacher; the home = the human body) and concludes that seeing merit and fault is the fault, being beyond both the merit.
Some twenty-eight qualities of the holy person (compassionate, harmless, forbearing, truthful ... friendly, merciful, wise).
The same list repeated in the Avadhūta Gītā.

An ancient tree made of karma with two seeds, a hundred roots, three trunks, five branches, five saps, eleven boughs, a nest of two birds, three barks and two fruits, cut down with the axe of knowledge sharpened by devotion to the teacher.

name: The many counts of the principles, reconciled

definitions.definition: The seers count the principles as nine, eleven, five, three, twenty-six, twenty-five, seven, six, four, seventeen, sixteen or thirteen; all are right, because the principles enter into one another and each speaker counts as he intends; the dispute itself arises from the Lord's powers and ceases with calm and self-control.

relations.note: a text-internal instance of reconciling divergent teachings by the intention of the speaker

name: One ultimate, many names

definitions.definition: Brahman, one without a second, is sung in many ways by the seers, so knowledge from a single teacher is not firm; the Veda's interpretations differ with natures.

The one from which words turn back is the Person of the Sāṃkhyas, the Brahman of the Vedāntins, the pure consciousness of the Vijñānavādins and the void of the Śūnyavādins; for the one established in the supreme it may be described with the terms no-self and emptiness; the external-object and consciousness doctrines are one for us.
The undivided understanding regarding Śiva, Viṣṇu, Śakti, the Sun and Gaṇeśa is right yoga; the one lord became fivefold.

notes: Text-layer statements that bear directly on ult:the-one (ṚV 1.164.46). Traditions that deny such equivalence (e.g. Buddhist schools on 'śūnya' as a name of a substantial ultimate) are not represented in these verses.

name: The mind as the cause of bondage and liberation

definitions.definition: Not people, gods, the body, planets, karma or time but the mind turns the wheel of saṃsāra; all disciplines culminate in its mastery (Bhikṣu Gītā); the mind attached to the guṇas binds, devoted to the Person frees (Kapila).

relations.note: the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha extends the mind's causality to the world itself

name: The world as the mind's projection

definitions.definition: The seen does not exist apart from consciousness; worlds arise from the mind's conceiving (saṅkalpa, manorājya) like dreams, whole lives occurring in a moment, worlds within a room, a rock or an atom; wiping away the seen is nirvāṇa.
All grasped by mind and senses is māyā, a mental creation; the three states are the mind's play like a whirling firebrand.

name: The seven stages of knowledge (jñāna-bhūmikā)

definitions.definition: Good desire, inquiry, thinning of mind, attainment of sattva, non-attachment, non-perception of objects and the reaching of the fourth; liberation lies beyond them; the seventh belongs to the jīvanmukta and the state beyond the fourth to the bodiless liberated.

relations.note: the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha pairs the seven stages of ignorance (3.117) with the seven of knowledge (3.118)

notes: The path map itself is pth:yoga-vasistha-seven-bhumikas (owned by U51).

definitions.definition: Seed-waking, waking, great waking, waking-dream, dream, dream-waking and deep sleep, each branching a hundredfold.
Peace, inquiry, contentment and holy company guard the door of liberation; cultivate all, or even one with all one's might, for when one is mastered the others follow.
Everything is won by rightly applied effort; fate is only one's former effort, overcome by present effort; reliance on fate is delusion.

name: The two seeds of the mind

definitions.definition: The tree of mind grows from two seeds, the vibration of prāṇa and firm conception (vāsanā); stilling either stills the mind, so yogins restrain the breath and give up vāsanās.
Consciousness-space, mind-space and elemental space; the latter two arise from consciousness-space.

name: The three great attitudes taught to Bhṛṅgīśa

definitions.definition: The great doer, the great enjoyer and the great renouncer: acting, enjoying and renouncing without ego, preference or notions of merit.

In the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha: the seventh stage; outwardly engaged, inwardly cool; mind 'dead' (manonāśa); one acts as custom requires, like one half-asleep. In the Aṣṭāvakra Gītā: the liberated is neither distracted nor absorbed, the same wherever he is. In the Rāma Gītā: living out prārabdha free of ego until merging.
The perfected one does not notice the body, which lives on while its karma lasts; though in the body he is not in it.
The destruction of ignorance, completion of human aims, is the state of liberation while living.

Tāmasa (with violence, pride, envy), rājasa (for objects, fame, power), sāttvika (to be rid of karma or because enjoined), all seeing difference; beyond them nirguṇa devotion, motiveless and unbroken.
Tāmasī, rājasī and sāttvikī devotion to the Goddess, and supreme devotion beyond them.
Sālokya, sārṣṭi, sāmīpya, sārūpya and oneness (ekatva), which pure devotees do not accept without service to the Lord.

name: The principles in the Kapila Gītā

definitions.definition: Twenty-four principles — five gross elements, five subtle elements, ten senses, and the fourfold inner instrument (mind, intellect, ego, citta) — with time as the twenty-fifth, identified with the Lord.

relations.note: one of the counts the Uddhava Gītā treats as valid by intention

definitions.definition: In the womb the jīva, from the seventh month conscious, remembers its past births and prays to the Lord, resolving to lift itself out; at birth it loses that knowledge. Death is the body's ceasing to function, birth the taking of 'I am this' toward a body.

name: Death and the hells in the Kapila Gītā

definitions.definition: The attached householder dies in torment, is led by Yama's messengers, suffers in hells the fruit of his deeds and returns to birth.

name: The paths of smoke and light (Kapila Gītā)

definitions.definition: Ritualists go by smoke to the moon and return; the desireless go by light to the Person; devotion is best.

notes: Parallels the Upaniṣadic pitṛyāna and devayāna (owned by U03).

name: The threefold consciousness (Rāma-hṛdaya)

definitions.definition: As space is threefold — the whole, the space delimited by a pond and the sky reflected in it — consciousness is the whole, the consciousness delimited by the intellect, and its reflection; agency belongs to the intellect with the reflection and is superimposed on the witness.

notes: Combines the Advaita 'limitation' and 'reflection' accounts in one image.

definitions.definition: Projection (vikṣepa), which creates the world, and veiling (āvaraṇa), which covers knowledge (Rāma to Lakṣmaṇa).

name: The nine means of devotion (Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa)

definitions.definition: Holy company; talk of the Lord's stories; singing his qualities; expounding his words; guileless service of the teacher as the Lord; virtuous conduct with steady worship; worship through his mantra; honouring devotees and seeing him in all with dispassion; inquiry into his nature — open to women, men and animals alike; the first leads to the rest in order.

relations.note: differs from the Bhāgavata's nine forms (hearing, singing, remembering, serving the feet, worship, bowing, servitude, friendship, self-offering)

definitions.definition: All selves in saṃsāra are paśus; Śiva is their lord (Paśupati), who binds them with the noose of māyā and alone frees them; he himself is bondage, binder, noose and bound (Īśvara Gītā).

The guru is Brahman, not other than the Self; 'gu' darkness, 'ru' its remover; the roots of meditation, worship, mantra and liberation are the guru's form, feet, word and grace; the teaching is secret, for the devoted only.
The avadhūta's many teachers; the self as its own teacher.

One who thinks himself free is free, one who thinks himself bound is bound (Aṣṭāvakra); bondage and liberation are said of the Lord only through the guṇas (Uddhava Gītā); bondage is bondage to vāsanā (Yoga Vāsiṣṭha).
